coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks
record.distance_note: The dry docks belong to the Pier 68/70 shipyard, next to Crane Cove Park and outside the tracked Pier 70 boundary (the Port's December 2025 park release describes new fencing along the Shipyard at the park's east side). Sources differ on when the shipyard closed: the Port's January and February 2026 memos say it operated until 2016 and has been inactive since, while a Port slide and Potrero View say 2017.

record.summary: Two Port-owned floating dry docks at Piers 68 & 70 -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- that the Port Commission's President and the Port's Executive Director declared an emergency over on 2025-12-08 after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding caused Dry Dock No. 2 to list. The Port is carrying out emergency stabilization repairs to Dry Dock No. 2 and plans to demolish and dispose of both structures; no source reports that demolition has begun. Potrero View reported in July 2026 that the Port has directed the engineering firm GHD to prepare preliminary demolition plans and expects initial plans "by next March" and a demolition contract tendered "the second half of 2027" (the paper's wording, not a Port document). The total estimated cost is $61.2M; as of February 2026 about $20.0M was identified ($18.5M of a requested supplemental appropriation plus $1.5M of BAE settlement funds) and the remaining $41.2M was anticipated in the FY2026-27 budget.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- two hand-traced hull outlines from satellite imagery, accurate to a few metres at best, not a surveyed footprint and not a Port or Assessor geometry. Which hull is Dry Dock No. 2 and which is the Eureka is inferred from their measured lengths against the 900 ft the Port memo gives for Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka lengths Mission Local (528 ft) and Potrero View (570 ft) give, which disagree (Marine Log, 2025-07-24, reporting the Port's request-for-proposals notice for the dry docks, lists the Eureka's length over pontoons as 528 ft and its overall length as 569 ft); no source read places them. The outlines cover the two floating hulls only, not the shipyard as a whole (the Port's July 11, 2017 release describes the shipyard lease as 'nearly 15 acres of land with numerous buildings, over 17 acres of submerged land, and Port-owned equipment'): the Pier 68 wharf arms, the quay, the cranes, the sheds and four unidentified floating tank sections west of the Eureka are left out. Needs replacement with a real digitized footprint if a Port GIS layer or the Dry Dock Memorandum's own site figure becomes available.
notes.digitized_from: Assessor lot: both hulls lie inside lot 9900068 (98% of the outline). DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' dataset (acdm-wktn), queried by lot number on 2026-10-10 and read again on 2026-10-11, lists Assessor lot 9900068 in block 9900 (lot 068), marked active, with a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02. The dataset's own description of its recorded-drop-date column reads 'This is the date that the documents related the to dropping/retiring of the parcel was recorded, as tracked by Public Works.' The same row has no map-drop date, is flagged active, and is on the Assessor's secured roll in the copy dated 2026-10-01. The dataset does not say why a recorded drop date and an active flag appear together, so this record states only what the row shows. The lot is the whole shipyard lot, not an outline of the two hulls: the traced hulls cover 18% of it. Port structures carry no street name in that dataset, so a search for PIER-numbered street names finds nothing. Outline: two hand-traced hull outlines -- Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock -- on Esri World Imagery (zoom 20, imagery captured 2025-08-29). The earlier placeholder box lay in open water north of the shipyard. Hulls were told apart by length. The Port Commission memo (Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09, PDF p. 3) says: 'DD2 is a 900-foot single-section steel floating dry dock constructed by the Bethlehem Steel Corporation in 1970.' Mission Local (2026-02-23) says: 'Dry Dock No. 2, which was built in 1970, ...' and 'The adjacent dry dock, Eureka, which was built in 1945, is 528 feet long'. Potrero View (2026-07-15) gives the Eureka as longer: 'Eureka Drydock is 570 feet.' The sources disagree on the Eureka's length (528 ft is 161 m; 570 ft is 174 m) and agree on its 1945 build. The large eastern hull measures about 283 m (Dry Dock No. 2: 900 ft is 274 m) and the central hull about 169 m including wing walls, so the central hull is the shorter dock whichever Eureka length is right. No source read says which hull sits where, so this match is Pier & Point's own inference. Still no Port GIS layer or site-plan figure to trace from.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Both hulls lie inside Assessor lot 9900068, the whole shipyard lot (DataSF Parcels, acdm-wktn, checked 2026-10-10 and again 2026-10-11), which this record does not use as an outline because the hulls cover only 18% of it. That row carries a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02 yet reads active; see 'Traced from' above.
notes.regulatory_context: Dry Dock No. 2 (a 900-foot floating dry dock built in 1970) developed excessive listing after hull tears and uncontrolled ballast-tank flooding in November 2025; the Port Commission President and Executive Director declared an emergency on 2025-12-08 (Port Commission memo, Calendar Item 9A, 2026-01-09). Port staff anticipate advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026 for Dry Dock No. 2 and the neighboring Eureka Dry Dock (a second floating dry dock at Piers 68/70, formerly USS Steadfast/AFDM-14, per Marine Log, 2025-07-24, reporting the Port's request-for-proposals notice, which calls it formerly known as Steadfast (AFDM 14) -- not the 1890 ferryboat Eureka at Hyde Street Pier/SF Maritime NHP). Total estimated cost of stabilization and disposal is $61.2M (Capital Planning Committee memo, 2026-02-09); see the record file for the funding breakdown and what remains unfunded.

costs.what: Not-to-exceed cost of the emergency repairs (welding and patching to reduce water intake, and stabilizing or removing the cranes on the Dry Dock No. 2 wing walls) under the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration, as stated in the memo dated 2026-01-09; the Port's Feb 9, 2026 memo to the Capital Planning Committee budgets the emergency work at $10,477,828 including a 20% contingency and a $200,000 reserve (Table 1), which is above this ceiling

Total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock (Phase 1A stabilization $8.6M + Dry Dock No. 2 disposal $27.4M + Eureka disposal $15.7M + $9.5M contingency, per the Port's Feb 9, 2026 cost table to the Capital Planning Committee; the Port's Jan 9, 2026 memo splits the same $61.2M differently, with Phase 1A at $7.2M and a $10.0M contingency); about $20.0M was identified as of Feb 2026 ($18.5M requested supplemental appropriation plus $1.5M of BAE settlement funds) and roughly $41.2M was anticipated in the FY2026-27 budget; no source read reports that either was adopted

open_questions: The Eureka Dry Dock's length is given as 528 feet by Mission Local (2026-02-23) and as 570 feet by Potrero View (2026-07-15) and by a slide in the Port's Feb 9, 2026 presentation to the Capital Planning Committee ("Eureka (570' x 125')"); the Port's January 2026 memo gives no length for it, and the sources conflict, so no length is shown as settled here. Both sources give 1945 as its build year and 900 feet and 1970 for Dry Dock No. 2.

Whether the Board of Supervisors adopted the $18.5M supplemental appropriation (ordinance File 251248, introduced Dec 16, 2025) and whether the remaining $41.2M was appropriated in the FY2026-27 budget is not reported in any source read; the Port's Feb 9, 2026 memo shows the $18.5M and $1.5M of BAE settlement funds as the first $20.0M of the $61.2M total.

Whether demolition will be completed "before winter storms" (a claim in an unsourced summary, not repeated in this record) is not supported by any primary source found; SFist (2026-03-05) reports it will likely be a year before the dry dock situation is resolved, and roughly $41.2M of the $61.2M total remained unfunded as of Feb 2026.

Has demolition of the dry docks begun, or has the Port advertised or awarded a demolition contract? As of 2026-10-12 no source read reports that demolition began, and no Port Commission item or Port contract notice was found reporting an advertisement or award; the July 2026 Potrero View report describes the design-build contract as still to come. The dry docks are therefore shown as existing, with demolition planned.
What becomes of BAE Systems' ship-repair operations at the adjacent Pier 70 shipyard once these dry docks are removed is not addressed in the sources reviewed here.
